claim: IMT on a home bought as the buyer's own permanent residence: marginal rates by bracket (2026)
value: Marginal / average rate at the top of each bracket: 0% / 0% up to 106 346 €; 2% / 0.5379% to 145 470 €; 5% / 1.7274% to 198 347 €; 7% / 3.8361% to 330 539 €; 8% to 660 982 €; 6% flat to 1 150 853 €; 7.5% flat above
source_title: Código do IMT, art. 17.º, n.º 1, al. a) (brackets per Lei 73-A/2025)

claim: IMT on a home not used as own permanent residence (e.g. second home), resident buyer (2026)
value: Marginal / average rate at the top of each bracket: 1% / 1% up to 106 346 €; 2% / 1.2689% to 145 470 €; 5% / 2.2636% to 198 347 €; 7% / 4.1578% to 330 539 €; 8% to 633 931 €; 6% flat to 1 150 853 €; 7.5% flat above
source_title: Código do IMT, art. 17.º, n.º 1, al. c)

claim: Non-resident buyers of an urban property used exclusively for housing pay IMT at a flat rate, with no exemption or reduction, unless an exception applies
source_title: Código do IMT, art. 17.º, n.º 10 (added by Decreto-Lei 97/2026, 20 May)
notes: Daniel to confirm: (1) start date: DL 97/2026 has no specific entry-into-force rule for this change, so the general 5-day rule gives 25 May 2026; (2) exception (a) 'tenha sido considerado residente para efeitos fiscais' - unclear whether past residence at any time (common for emigrants) qualifies. Do not state either point as settled until confirmed.

claim: Exceptions to the flat non-resident IMT rate
value: (a) buyer has been considered a Portuguese tax resident; (b) buyer becomes tax resident within 2 years of the purchase; (c) home let for housing within 6 months at a rent within the DL 97/2026 caps, for at least 36 months in the first 5 years. In (b) and (c) the difference is refunded on request within 6 months
source_title: Código do IMT, art. 17.º, n.os 10 a 12; Decreto-Lei 97/2026
notes: Official DR text: https://files.diariodarepublica.pt/1s/2026/05/09700/0001400040.pdf . See notes on pt-imt-nonresident-flat.
